Treat each user’s HR@10 as a binary outcome; pair baseline/intervention results on identical users and candidate sets. For category c, estimate Δc = mean(hit_intervention − hit_baseline). Report percentage-point differences, discordant win/loss counts, and 95% paired-bootstrap intervals, resampling users with both outcomes together. Exact McNemar tests can supplement category estimates when discordances are sparse; separate marginal confidence intervals do not estimate uncertainty in the difference. [Paired comparison methods](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume5/rifkin04a/rifkin04a.pdf). For this benchmark, macro improvement is Δmacro = (ΔMovies + ΔIndustrial + ΔElectronics + ΔCDs)/4. Bootstrap within each category, retaining 200 paired users, then average the four differences in every replicate. This estimates uncertainty over users within these four fixed categories, assuming independent users; do not treat 99 negatives as independent observations or four categories as evidence about all domains.

Predeclare checkpoint evaluation frequency, selection metric, tie-breaking, stopping rule, and comparable search opportunities; retain the 200-epoch/200-batch caps. Log all inspected checkpoints and interventions. For a sampling-only comparison, hold other settings fixed. Selecting checkpoints and interventions on the same validation data creates optimism; ordinary bootstrap intervals do not correct adaptive selection. Describe them as exploratory, conditional intervals, and reserve confirmation for the host’s untouched final evaluation. [Selection bias](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [adaptive reuse](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629).

Seed 42 supports reproducibility but cannot estimate training-seed variance; user bootstrap cannot establish robustness across retraining. [Seed sensitivity](https://aclanthology.org/D17-1035/). Fixed candidates control comparison noise, but conclusions concern this sampled-ranking protocol, not full-catalog HR@10; sampled metrics can change model ordering. [Sampled recommendation metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).
